# Draft:Canadian Transportation Museum & Heritage Village

The Canadian Transportation Museum & Heritage Village (also known as CTMHV or Heritage Village) is an automotive museum and pioneer village in Kingsville, Ontario, Canada, situated on a 100 acre site. It is home to over 80 vehicles ranging from an early 1800s log wagon to a 1992 Dodge Viper, and over 20 historic buildings. The transportation museum section features a permanent exhibit of motorcycles, conceived by the Two Wheels Only Foundation of Ontario Riders. CTMHV is also home to the only EMS museum in Canada.
History
The museum is operated by the Historic Vehicle Society of Ontario (HVSO) which was founded in 1954. Meeting were originally held in members' houses but as their membership grew, they began meeting at the Roseland Women’s Institute Hall. The club purchased the Borden Dairy Building in downtown Windsor in the early 1960s, then in 1973 they purchased the current property. The main museum building originally only consisted of what is now the banquet hall. In 2001, through a donation from the family of Don Beneteau, an expansion was added which consists of the 50s Diner, the lobby, the gift shop, and the three museum salons.
Heritage Village
The Heritage Village contains over 20 historic buildings that were relocated from around Essex County and Chatham-Kent.
Amherstburg Cabin, circa 1820 - Moved to the Village in 1980. Originally located at the intersection of Park and King Street in Amherstburg, near Fort Malden.
Boudreau Cabin, 1835 - First building moved to the Village in 1974. Originally located in Raleigh Township near Tilbury.
Clark Cabin, 1826 - Moved to the Village in 1978. Originally located in Cottam on the South side of Talbot Road on lot 126.
Waggott House, 1869 - Moved to the Village in 1976. Originally located in Kingsville.
Barber Shop and Cobbler Shop, circa 1930 - Moved to the Village in 1976. Originally located on Gesto Rd in Essex.
Blacksmith Shop, 1857 - Moved to the the Village in 2024. Originally located on Lot 14 of Concession 3 North in Anderdon Township which is now part of Amherstburg.
Doctor’s Office, 1892 - Moved to the Village in 1990. Originally located at 15 Queen Street in Harrow.
Masonic Lodge
Sugar Shack
Ross Cabin, 1848 - Moved to the Village in 1986. Originally located in Cottam on County Rd 34.
Olinda General Store, 1840 - Moved to the Village 1982. Originally located on Olinda side road near Ruthven.
Woodslee Jail, 1895 - Moved to the Village in 1997. Originally located in Woodslee which is now part of Lakeshore.
Print Shop
Town Hall
S No.1 Gosfield South School House, 1907 - Moved to the Village 1975. Originally located on Highway 20 towards Kingsville, between Arner Townline and McCain Side Road.
Bethel United Church, 1885 - Moved to the Village 1978. Originally located on Arner Townline and the 6th Concession.
Tecumseh Train Station, 1860 - Moved to the Village in 1976. Originally located in Tecumseh on Tecumseh Road East.
Jack Miner Homestead, 1889 - Moved to the Village 2003. Originally located on 332 Road 3 W in Kingsville, which is now the location of the Jack Miner Migratory Bird Sanctuary.
Holden Cabin, 1864 - Moved to the Village in 1995. Originally located on 6th Concession in Sandwich East Township.
Whelan Cabin, 1843 - Moved to the Village in 2008. Originally located on Lot 3 on the 3rd Concession between Texas Road and Alma Street in Anderdon Township which is now part of Amherstburg.
